risks.description: POST /approve may apply the payment effect and then stall past the client's timeout, leaving the caller unable to tell whether the approval landed while the effect is durably present.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires the approval to be recorded durably; the uncertain code path applies the effect then sleeps STALL_S before answering, so a timed-out caller has no signal.

risks.description: Two approvals of the same invoice arriving simultaneously could each append a payment, producing more than one payment for a single invoice.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; the nonidempotent path appends a payment on every call with no status guard, and the failed gen-idempotent-approve run already showed payments>1.

risks.description: A client retry after an ambiguous timeout could apply the effect a second time, double-recording the approval/payment.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; the uncertain path stalls even on retry, so a client cannot know its first attempt succeeded and will retry.

risks.description: The endpoint may return 200 approved (and claim persisted:true) while never writing the durable store, so a re-read of persisted state still shows pending.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 requires approval state to survive a re-read of persisted state; the ui_lies path omits _save().

risks.description: An approval request with no actor/body could fail to record a durable approval or record it inconsistently.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires the approval to be recorded durably regardless of caller-supplied actor detail.

scenarios.title: Approve that stalls past client timeout still leaves exactly one durable approval
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the uncertain/ambiguous-effect path: a client that times out waiting for /approve must still be able to learn, from the durable oracle, that the approval landed exactly once and unambiguously.
scenarios.rationale: The uncertain defect applies the effect then sleeps past any sane client timeout; an HTTP 200 is not evidence, so the load-bearing check is a durable state read after the client would have given up.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a unique invoice id INV-A2W2-TMO touched by no other scenario; state.py is queried for that id only, so it cannot observe or contaminate other invoices. No reset command is approved, so isolation is by unique id rather than cleanup.
expected_observations: After the client-side timeout window, the durable store reports INV-A2W2-TMO status=approved approvals=1 payments=1
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows payments=2 or approvals=2 (effect applied more than once)
Durable store still shows status=pending after the effect window (effect silently lost)

scenarios.title: Retrying an approval after an ambiguous timeout does not double-record
scenarios.purpose: A client that times out and safely retries the same approval must not cause a second payment; the durable store must show exactly one approval after both attempts.
scenarios.rationale: Distinct from sequential idempotency: this models the realistic retry-after-timeout the uncertain path forces, where the client cannot know the first attempt succeeded. Verified only via the durable oracle.
scenarios.isolation_note: Unique invoice id INV-A2W2-RETRY, inspected by id only; no other scenario touches it. No approved reset command exists, so isolation is via the unique id.
expected_observations: After the initial timed-out approval and one retry, the durable store shows INV-A2W2-RETRY approvals=1 payments=1
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows payments=2 or approvals=2 after the retry

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice record a single payment
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the race: two approvals of the same invoice arriving at once must collapse to exactly one durable approval and one payment, exercising the lock/guard rather than the sequential path.
scenarios.rationale: Sequential idempotency (already covered) does not exercise concurrent contention on the shared record; a missing or mis-scoped guard shows up only under true parallelism, verified by the durable oracle.
scenarios.isolation_note: Unique invoice id INV-A2W2-CONC, queried by id only. No approved reset command, so isolation is by unique id.
expected_observations: Durable store shows INV-A2W2-CONC approvals=1 payments=1 after two simultaneous approvals
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows payments=2 or approvals=2 (both concurrent calls applied the effect)

scenarios.title: A 200-approved response must agree with an independent re-read of persisted state
scenarios.purpose: Directly exercise AC-APPROVAL-002: after the endpoint answers approved, an independent process re-reading the durable store must also see approved — catching a UI/backend disagreement where the response lies about persistence.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-002 is about survival across a re-read, not the write instant. The oracle is a separate process reading the file, so a response that reports persisted:true while never calling _save() is exposed. Restart is deliberately NOT used because the fixture reseeds the store on boot.
scenarios.isolation_note: Unique invoice id INV-A2W2-REREAD, queried by id only. No approved reset command, so isolation is via the unique id.
expected_observations: Endpoint returns 200 approved AND an independent re-read of the durable store shows INV-A2W2-REREAD status=approved approvals=1 payments=1
forbidden_observations: Endpoint returns approved but the durable re-read still shows status=pending or approvals=0

scenarios.title: Approval with no actor supplied is still recorded durably exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise missing input: an approve request with an empty body must still durably record exactly one approval (with a defaulted actor), never silently drop it or record it twice.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-001 promises durable recording regardless of caller-supplied actor detail; the empty-body path defaults actor to unknown and must still persist one approval.
scenarios.isolation_note: Unique invoice id INV-A2W2-NOACTOR, queried by id only. No approved reset command, so isolation is via the unique id.
expected_observations: Durable store shows INV-A2W2-NOACTOR status=approved approvals=1 payments=1 after an approval with no actor
forbidden_observations: Durable store still shows status=pending (approval dropped)
Durable store shows approvals=2 or payments=2

assumptions: state.py reads the durable store file (the intended oracle) and accepts an invoice-id argument, which counts as an allowed extra argument on the approved command.
Invoices are created on first touch, so each scenario can use a private, never-before-touched invoice id and inspect only that id, giving isolation without any reset command (none is approved).
Only one defect mode is active per run; the scenario set is chosen so that whichever mode is live (nonidempotent, ui_lies, or uncertain) is caught by at least one durable-state check.
The uncertain path's STALL_S default is ~8s, so a client timeout_s of 3 plus a ~9s wait before the oracle read reliably observes the post-stall durable state.
unresolved_questions: AC-APPROVAL-002 says approval state must survive a re-read of persisted state, but the service's main() unlinks and reseeds store.json on every boot; this makes it impossible to verify survival across a genuine process restart (restart_service would always show a wiped store). Is restart-survival in scope, or is 'survives a re-read' satisfied purely by an independent-process read of the file while the service stays up? I verified only the latter.

Neither acceptance criterion states whether approval requires authorization or an approval-required gate (who may approve, or a second approver). No auth is present in the changed code, so authorization/approval_required situations were not exercised — confirm whether they are promised anywhere before trusting the endpoint.

No approved command resets or seeds the durable store, so scenario isolation relies entirely on unique invoice ids; if the harness needs a clean store between waves, an approved reset command would be required.
